doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Young white banjo players and the age of Marrero's banjo
summary: Marrero offers to help Allen, talks about Bill Huntington and John Schaff, who play without knowing how to hold a banjo, and how old his instrument is.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I see, I figure the easy way is the best way. I mean for you when you make your own place something you can kill. That's right. The thing that I know of, I don't know everything, but the thing that I do know, I'd be glad to help you out on it. I had a pretty good little band of players. You remember him, Bill Huntington? He was in the store Monday night.
Yeah. When the spotter came by. Well him, Bill Huntington.

Man he played like hell. He didn't know how to hold a banjo. There's another white kid called John Shaft, you ever met him? Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He didn't know a thing either. He was in the banjo bones. Yeah, well he can play some banjo bones. Yeah. But them boys, they're young, they come, you see.
You're using this as an Epiphone recording.
How old do you think this is? Oh man, that's a band of older than you are. Oh yeah. I had older 20 years myself.
Yeah. Oh God, my boy, my God, stop playing. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
